reader.requirement: At 1985 the indexed-file FD clauses (BLOCK CONTAINS, RECORD in its three forms, LABEL RECORDS, VALUE OF, DATA RECORDS) are accepted in any order after file-name-1, each at most once.

edition-consulted.switches: ConstructRegistry LabelRecordsRemoved2002 (and the VALUE OF / DATA RECORDS siblings): accepted at 1985, refused from 2002

reader.edition-search: the order itself is fileDescriptionClause+ in the grammar, with no predicate; the edition enters only through the removal gates of the three 1985-only clauses.
reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: yes: LABEL RECORDS, VALUE OF and DATA RECORDS exist only at 1985; ordering freedom is the same at every edition
reader.witnesses-cover: part: g85_bf22_03 covers one reversed order of DATA, LABEL, RECORD CONTAINS, BLOCK; not covered: VALUE OF, RECORD VARYING ... DEPENDING, BLOCK ... TO ... CHARACTERS, a repeated clause

reader.notes: The grammar takes the FD clauses as an unordered repetition and FileDescriptionFormats decides admission per clause, so any permutation is accepted; repetition is refused by UnrepeatedElements. COBOL2423 cites §2023:13.4.5.2 at --std 85 (wording only).

refuter.evidence: The composite skeleton (§1985 V, indexed FD) puts IS EXTERNAL and IS GLOBAL among 'the clauses which follow file-name-1'. g1.cob --std 85: FD XF LABEL RECORDS ARE STANDARD IS GLOBAL BLOCK CONTAINS 2 RECORDS IS EXTERNAL -> accepted, R=01AAAAAAAA. g4.cob: DATA RECORD, VALUE OF FILE-ID IS data-name, LABEL, RECORD CONTAINS in that order -> accepted. Refusal half for clauses outside the indexed format: g2.cob LINAGE and g3.cob CODE-SET in an indexed FD -> COBOL2604 'not a clause of Format 2 (relative-or-indexed)' (cites §2023, wording only).
